verdicts.why: Doom's takeover of Octopus's realm has already happened when it is stated on screen in #62 (Doom mentioned, Ock in flashback); the stage is not earlier than what it says, so moving it to #63 is an 'either works' change.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#57
value.text: The Chameleon turns on the Kingpin and the Insidious Six to help Kragov free the Red Skull, who then traps the Six.
value.on_a_card_about_b: One of Doctor Octopus's Six, who betrays the team.
value.on_b_card_about_a: A teammate in the Six, whom the Chameleon betrays.

verdicts.why: Real turn: in #57 the Chameleon leaves the Six and helps Kragov free the Red Skull, who traps Kingpin's Six. But he steals the keys while still with the Six (Kingpin then wins them), and in this arc the Kingpin, not Ock, runs the Six, so 'Leads the Six' is unsupported.

Wong appears only in #28, where he fights Mordo's cult and guards the portal while Strange and Spider-Man face Dormammu; nothing passes between Wong and Dormammu, and 'The demon Wong fights' is false.
In #1 the Lizard attacks Eddie, Eddie overhears Margaret say Curt is the Lizard, and the next morning he and Jameson knock on Connors's door to find him human. The connection starts here.
In #38 Venom attacks his old boss Jameson at the Bugle, then turns on Spider-Man until Iron Man stops him and he flees; he does not overpower Spider-Man and leave with Kafka.
In #32 Felicia turns Peter down, then happily agrees when Jason asks her to dinner, and the two begin dating; the #40 engagement is later.

value.title: The Spectacular Spider-Man#5
value.text: Pushed by Norman Osborn, a reluctant Otto runs the experiment that turns Flint Marko into the Sandman.
value.on_a_card_about_b: A crook Otto's experiment turns to sand.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The scientist whose experiment turns him to sand.

verdicts.why: The connection clearly starts on screen in #5, so it gets a stage there. Marko is a Hammerhead recruit and Otto works for the same operation, so they are on the same side, not enemies. The #11 text should then hold only the Sinister Six (e.g. 'Otto brings the Sandman into his Sinister Six.').

value.title: The Spectacular Spider-Man#6
value.text: Pushed by Hammerhead, a wary Otto bonds Alex O'Hirn to the rhino armor.
value.on_a_card_about_b: A thug Otto bonds to the rhino armor.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The scientist who bonds him to his armor.

verdicts.why: The connection clearly starts on screen in #6, so it gets a stage there. O'Hirn is a willing Hammerhead recruit, so they are on the same side, not enemies. The #11 text should then hold only the breakout and the Six (e.g. 'The Rhino helps break Otto out of prison and joins his Sinister Six.').
In #58 Kragov becomes Electro while facing Spider-Man, Silver Sable and the Warriors; the Kingpin is not in the episode (listed only for the tie-in comic), so nothing passes between them there.

In #48 Black Cat and Spider-Man go to Whistler for a weapon, and Whistler, Terri and they hunt Morbius, find Miriam and later stop her at the club; Blade disarms them and turns them down, so Whistler never joins 'Felicia and Blade'.
Sources disagree on where #11 leaves them: the Marvel Database synopsis has the Kingpin refuse to pay and the Hobgoblin betray him and go back after Fisk within #11, so 'enemy' is not shown wrong.
In #40 the Hobgoblin confronts the Kingpin, who accepts his offer of partnership and plans the heist with him while plotting a double-cross: a clear turn with no stage.

In #42 Tombstone teams with his cellmate Richard, who has his father frame Robbie and send him to their prison, and the Kingpin's undercover man breaks Tombstone and Richard out: the Kingpin acts directly for his wife's kidnapper.
In #50 Mysterio reveals the Kingpin funded his automatons for his plan to destroy Spider-Man, and Mysterio stays with Miranda as the studio explodes; a stated tie plus his death.
In #50 it is Miranda who plans to swap bodies with Mary Jane; Mysterio rebuilt her and reveals the machine was never designed to work, so the current text gives the plan to the wrong person.

The current text is wrong, but the fix is too: Mary Jane is lost in limbo and not in #45, and May moving in with Anna is between May and Anna, not May and Mary Jane. Nothing passes between the two there, so the stage goes.

In #45 Kraven explains he saved Mariah from a deadly virus with his serum and she turned feral; Connors's serum only partly reverses it and she chooses to stay as she is and leaves with Kraven. He is not out to stop her, and the #7 backstory is not new here.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#55
value.text: The Chameleon poses as the husband of Dr. Groitzig's daughter to steal the evidence about Peter's parents, then leads Spider-Man into the Insidious Six's trap.

verdicts.why: Right move: the #57 text is about the Chameleon and the Kingpin, while in #55 the Chameleon, impersonating the daughter's husband Karl, takes the evidence and leads Spider-Man into the Six's trap. But she is the scientist's daughter, not 'a witness'.
In #51 Peter and Mary Jane ask Connors to give her away, and three lizards grown from his DNA kidnap him and he becomes the Lizard again; nothing blames stress.
In #61 the Lizard attacks Spider-Man, Iron Man and Mister Fantastic restore Connors's mind, and Connors sides with Spider-Man's team: a clear new turn with no stage.

In #14 Mysterio steals for the Master Planner; Spider-Man arrests a robot double, and the Tinkerer, annoyed that Beck wanted the duplicates in his likeness, tells the real Beck he can come out. Something passes between them, and they are free and working again after #10.
In #23, after seeing Peter with Felicia, Mary Jane seeks reassurance and is then seen out on a date with Harry, which devastates Peter: the break happens here, not in #41.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#35
value.text: After Spider-Man saves her from the Kingpin's base, Mary Jane gives back Harry's engagement ring and tells Spider-Man that she loves someone else.

verdicts.why: Real missing turn: in #35 she hands back Harry's ring and tells Spider-Man she doesn't love Harry and thinks she loves somebody else. She does not name Peter on screen, so 'knowing she loves Peter' goes.
By #41 Liz remarks that Mary Jane and Peter finally got together; the turn to Harry (#23) and the broken engagement (#35) happen earlier, so the #41 text should hold only what happens there.
In #41 Mary Jane says Harry thinks Peter betrayed him, Harry is cold to Peter at his party, and by the end Harry wants nothing to do with Peter: a clear falling-out with no stage.
At the end of #45 Peter and Harry decide to share a flat again to help each other through their problems: a reconciliation before #49.
In #53 Liz appeals to Harry to go back to Ravencroft and he stands down, and the wedding goes ahead, so 'out to kill him' is no longer true from this stage on.

In #53 Peter visits Fisk, who offers to pay for the wedding because Peter once saved his life from the Hobgoblin, and Peter accepts though he knows Fisk is the Kingpin; Fisk later sends the Mega-Slayer to the church.
In #45 the stalker is Mariah, turned feral by the serum Kraven gave her, and Spider-Man, Black Cat and Kraven give her Connors's serum, which partly restores her.

In #44 Landon recreates the serum but nothing passes between him and Spider-Man; in #47 Landon and the Shocker take Morbius to study him, Spider-Man and Black Cat interrupt, and Morbius drains Landon.

value.option: Order X-Men '97 S1 after Spider-Man (1994) in the Spider-Verse, so this becomes the last stage

verdicts.why: A stage is never earlier than what it says has happened: the X-Men '97 #10 scene shows Peter and Mary Jane together after he set out to find her at the end of Spider-Man (1994) #65, so it cannot sort before their blind date. It is a real on-screen event, so it is not dropped.
In #65 that world's Ben brings out the real Peter in Spider-Carnage, who cannot overcome the symbiote and jumps into an unstable portal that destroys him; the stage leaves out his death.
Not shown: the Marvel Database lists the planet as Battleworld for #61 to #63, and no source shows the name is never said on screen.
